environment: This repository is Pilot, a CLI and Admin backend that manages Frappe benches. Agents run commands against local benches, development hosts, staging and production. The access policy is in llm/engineering-playbook/references/environments.md.

Each developer declares their own development, staging and production hosts, sites and cloud accounts in additional environment entries in their personal settings. Those entries decide the tier of a target.

Development tier: local bench sites ending in .localhost, the test.local site, localhost services, local containers, and any host, VM or cloud resource declared as development. Agents may act freely there.
allow: Commands against the development tier: local bench sites (*.localhost, test.local), localhost services, local containers, and hosts or VMs declared as development. This includes pilot, bench, ssh, systemctl, nginx, database and deploy commands on those targets.
soft_deny: Any write, restart, deploy, migrate, update, data patch or bench, site or host change on a target declared as staging, or on a host reached through one. Read-only inspection is fine. Block unless the developer approved this exact action in the conversation.
Provider API calls that create, delete, resize or attach paid cloud resources, even in development, unless the developer approved this exact action.
Running the test suite against any site other than test.local, or dropping and reinstalling a site that is not test.local.
hard_deny: Any command, SSH session, API call, script or file copy that reaches a target declared as production, including through jump hosts, ProxyCommand chains or scripts.
Any command against a host, IP address, domain, site, bucket or cloud account that is not declared as development or staging. Treat undeclared targets as production.
Printing, copying or committing secrets, private keys, tokens or .env content from any environment.
